title: Perfect Investigation
verdict: Every lie answered, down to the code on the alarm.
narrative: You put it to {accused} over his own kitchen table: the code, the handbrake, the job sheet, the driver. He finishes his tea before he answers.
The roadster is stopped at Harwich an hour before its ferry sails, still wrapped in the Hale House dust sheet.
Augustus Hale comes downstairs for the first time in a month to see it rolled back into its bay.

title: True Criminal
verdict: The right name, and enough to hold it.
narrative: {accused} is charged before the insurers close the file.
The case holds, though his counsel makes much of the lies you never broke.
The roadster is traced to Rotterdam in the autumn and comes home the long way.

title: Wrong Suspect
verdict: A careful case, built around the wrong person.
narrative: Your case against {accused} has a motive, a lie and a night on the timeline. It is still wrong.
The charges are dropped. By then the roadster has changed hands twice on the continent.
The file is reopened in the winter and handed to somebody else.

title: Innocent Person Accused
narrative: {accused} is arrested in front of half the Motor Club.
The charges are dropped within the week. The club doesn't forget.
Chassis four of four is never seen in Ridgeway again.

title: Criminal Escapes
verdict: The car rolled away in the dark, and so did the case.
narrative: At nine o'clock the insurers write the roadster off.
Whoever pushed it down the drive knew the house, the car and the codes, and knew you wouldn't get there in time.
Case #050 is filed under Unsolved. A Castellane Sprint appears at a Geneva auction three years later, chassis number filed off.
